title: Gradient
blurb: A fullscreen fragment shader and nothing else — the smallest thing in the repo that renders. Sweeps a cosine palette around the polar angle, with a breathing ring on the radius.

title: Cloud form
blurb: A real HTML form with no background of its own, over a canvas drawing the cloud that serves as its chrome. A ResizeObserver feeds the form's measured rect to the shader, so the silhouette tracks the DOM through any reflow, and focus swells the cloud.

title: Mutation
blurb: A raymarched arm coming apart, after the Tetsuo transformation. Masses erupt along the limb through smooth unions, and the tissue is separated into cells by a Voronoi projected cylindrically around the arm — muscle, bruise, fat and something colder, each cell picking one. Backscattered light through the thin parts gives it the volume a flat 2D field cannot. A slider drives the whole thing.

title: Endoluminal intake
blurb: The same cylinder as the arm, turned inside out and looked at rather than travelled down. The camera does not move and neither does the relief: nodules sit on Voronoi seed points, which scatter far more evenly than noise, and stay where they are. The whole wall moves as one on a heartbeat — a strong pulse, a weaker one after it, then a pause — because a wave with a spatial phase slides features through frame and reads as peristalsis instead. The same waveform flushes the tissue redder on systole, so the beat reads as blood arriving. Blue veins branch under the mucosa as actual trees rather than noise contours, so no branch ever closes a loop and every tip tapers away. A long HTML form sits on it with no panel of its own: the shader congests the wall where the form presses — pinched pale at the rim, pooling dark inside — and cuts every field into it as a wet depression while pushing the button out as a blanched welt. The controls carry no CSS background, border or focus ring at all; red-and-white type sits straight on the tissue. Scrolling does not move the tissue past the camera — it hands the scroll position to the shader and moves the camera along the wall.
